subject: Life Skills
title: Meeting Manners
description: A micro-lesson that makes Meeting Manners usable.

hook.text: The average professional spends 31 hours a month in meetings. Most could be emails. The rest need rules.

buildup.text: Showing up late signals 'my time matters more than yours.' Two minutes early is the unwritten standard.

discovery.text: Mute when not speaking. Do not type loudly. These tiny acts show you respect the current speaker.

twist.text: Jumping in right after someone finishes feels eager but rude. A two-second pause signals you actually listened.

climax.text: Summarize what you heard before adding your point. 'So you are saying X — here is how I see it.'

punchline.text: Arrive early, mute often, pause before speaking.

quiz.question: What does pausing before responding in a meeting signal?
options: You are unsure of your answer
You were actually listening to the speaker
You want someone else to respond first
